jobs.title: Director, Data and Insights
jobs.description:
At Pacific Blue Cross, we're committed to improving health and wellbeing for British Columbians. As our Director, Data & Insights Office, you'll have a rare opportunity to build and shape a critical enterprise capability that will influence how decisions are made across the organization for years to come.

Reporting to the Vice President, Information Technology & Enterprise Transformation, you will lead the development of PBC's enterprise data, analytics, and AI strategy, helping transform data from an operational asset into a strategic advantage. Working closely with executive leaders and business partners, you will establish the foundations that enable trusted insights, stronger decision-making, and greater organizational agility.
This is more than a data leadership role. It is an opportunity to drive meaningful transformation across the organization. You'll influence enterprise priorities, champion innovation, and create a culture where data empowers teams to better serve members, improve operational performance, and deliver on PBC's long-term strategic objectives.

We're looking for a strategic and collaborative leader who is energized by building new capabilities, navigating complexity, and creating lasting organizational impact. You bring the vision to define what's possible, the influence to bring people together, and the execution focus to turn strategy into measurable results.

If your experience includes roles such as Director of Data & Analytics, Director of Business Intelligence, Head of Data & Insights, Director of Data Governance, Director of Enterprise Analytics, Director of Data Strategy, Director of AI & Analytics, Chief Data Officer, Analytics Director, Enterprise Data Leader, or similar leadership positions, and you've successfully leveraged data, analytics, and emerging technologies to drive business outcomes within industries such as healthcare, insurance, financial services, telecommunications, consulting, retail, or other complex, data-driven environments

Key Details

Position Title:
Director, Data and Insights
Work Arrangement:
Hybrid - 3 days in the office and 2 days’ work from home
Office Location:
4250 Canada Way, Burnaby, BC V5G 4W6
Classification:
Exempt
Salary Range:
$138,000 - $208,000 ( Pacific Blue Cross’ compensation program is built on a pay-for-performance philosophy, rewarding both individual and organizational achievements. We determine starting salaries by considering a variety of factors, including relevant skills, education, experience, and internal equity, ensuring compensation decisions are consistent, equitable, and reflective of each candidate’s unique background and qualifications)
Incentive Compensation Plan (ICP bonus) per year based on performance:
Up to 15.00%

Total Rewards Highlights:

Flexible working hours of 7.5 hours per day, Monday to Friday (i.e., 37.5 hours per week).
Paid vacation starts at 4 weeks per year and increases with years of service.
Generous benefits, including extended health, dental, and life insurance; depending on the plan that you choose, these benefit premiums can be 100% paid by PBC.
PBC contributes the equivalent of 8% of your base salary to a Defined Contribution pension plan. No employee contribution or matching is required, giving you more take-home pay

Pacific Blue Cross (PBC) has been British Columbia’s leading benefits provider for over 80 years. We are an independent, not-for-profit society with strong roots in BC’s health care system.

Why You'll Love Working Here

Retiree Benefits plan that is available to employees who have at least 10 years of service with PBC and have reached the age of 55.
Access to an onsite fitness center and cafeteria, along with employee events and activities designed to foster a collaborative and engaging work environment.
Access to virtual doctors/counsellors 24/7 via our Employee Family Assistance Program!
Learning and development opportunities
Wellness initiatives and onsite amenities

Drive enterprise data strategy and modernization initiatives, helping advance data quality, reporting consistency, analytics capabilities, and AI readiness across business and technology teams.
Enable data-driven decision-making by improving access to trusted information, empowering leaders with actionable insights, and expanding self-service analytics capabilities.
Champion analytics and AI innovation, identifying high-value opportunities that improve operational effectiveness, enhance member experiences, and deliver measurable business value.
Influence organizational transformation by fostering data literacy, building strategic partnerships, and creating alignment between business priorities, technology investments, and enterprise outcomes.

Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) with a major in Business, Data Science, Statistics, or an equivalent discipline, including or supplemented by courses in leadership/supervision.
Strong expertise in data governance, analytics, and emerging AI applications.
10 - 12 years of related experience in data and analytics including the application of insights into decision-making and/or automated processes.
7+ years of experience in progressively senior leadership positions.
Excellent project and change management skills.
Ability to translate business drivers and challenges into data insights and initiatives.

Key Competencies

Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to identify, analyze, and resolve challenges, driving solutions through to completion
Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship building skills with both business and technical stakeholders.

jobs.title: Senior Director Benefits Governance
jobs.description:
As Senior Director, Benefits Governance, you define the strategic direction and oversee the evolution of the Bank’s employee benefits offering. As a recognized leader in the field, you act as a trusted advisor to the leadership teams and contribute to attracting, engaging, and retaining talent through competitive, equitable, and business-aligned programs.

You lead a team of experts responsible for areas including group insurance, attendance and absence management, and occupational health and safety. You also ensure innovation, sound governance, regulatory compliance, and the effective management of investments related to the programs under your responsibility.

This strategic role gives you the opportunity to make a significant impact across the organization through your leadership, collaborative approach, and ability to mobilize stakeholders.

Your Role

Lead and develop a small team of specialized experts.

Act as a recognized leader and internal subject matter expert on employee benefits matters, supporting business priorities as well as talent attraction, engagement, and retention.

Define and evolve the strategies, policies, programs, and technology platforms that support the employee benefits offering.

Advise leadership teams on complex and strategic matters.

Monitor market trends to ensure a competitive and innovative benefits offering.

Collaborate with business partners to evolve programs based on the needs of the Bank and its employees.

Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, governance standards, and risk management practices.

Manage budgets, measure program performance, and drive value creation.

Develop and maintain strategic relationships with vendors and external partners.

Represent the Bank with external organizations and partners when required.

Your Team

Reporting to the Senior director, Wellness, Benefits & Recognition, within the Human Experience and Performance (HEP) sector, you will be part of the Total Rewards team, consisting of approximately 45 colleagues.

Our team is recognized for its deep expertise and innovative approach, focused on transforming and advancing total rewards practices.

We are committed to providing flexibility to support your quality of life through a hybrid work model and flexible work arrangements.

Prerequisites

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline and 7 to 10 years of experience, or a master’s degree and a minimum of 5 years of experience.

Recognized expertise in the design and evolution of employee benefits, health and wellness, retirement programs, or related fields.

Demonstrated leadership experience in managing and developing specialized teams.

Ability to define strategic directions and lead complex initiatives in a transforming environment.

Excellent influencing, communication, and advisory skills with senior leadership and a broad range of stakeholders.

Strong analytical, decision-making, and financial management capabilities, including the use of data to inform recommendations.

Proven ability to innovate, mobilize teams, and build lasting partnerships internally and externally.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to carry out regularly tasks that require the use of IT apps and tools unavailable in French.
Required skills: Business Alignment, Critical Thinking, Data-Driven Decision-Making, Decision Making, Diversity & Inclusion, Emotional Intelligence, Innovation Management, Learning Agility, Managerial Courage, Mobilization, Partner Development, Resiliency, Risk Management, Strategic Vision, Strategy Execution, Stress Management

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. jobs.title: Director, Technology Communications & Organizational Change Management (14 month contract)
jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Technology Communications & Change (14 month contract)
to lead two interconnected functions: Technology Communications and Technology Organizational Change Management (OCM). This role establishes the strategic direction, governance, standards, and priorities for how Technology communicates with employees, leaders, and external audiences, and how technology-driven change is assessed, planned, adopted, sustained, and measured across a complex portfolio of initiatives.

As a trusted advisor to Technology leadership, you will translate complex priorities into clear narratives, embed the employee perspective into critical decisions, and create the conditions required for successful organizational change. You will oversee portfolio-level change planning, strengthen sponsor and leadership capability, proactively identify change risk and organizational saturation, and ensure priority initiatives are supported by robust impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, learning, readiness, adoption, sustainment, and measurement practices that drive successful business outcomes.

What You Will Do

Define and drive the strategic direction for Technology communications and organizational change management, aligned with Technology priorities and business objectives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to Technology leadership, providing guidance on executive communications, employee engagement, organizational change, and stakeholder alignment.
Shape and oversee Technology's communications governance model, ensuring communication activities are coordinated, strategic, and aligned across the organization.
Partner closely with Corporate Communications, HR, Enterprise Change, Learning, Technology leaders, and business stakeholders to align messaging, coordinate change activity, and reduce communication overlap and fatigue.
Provide organizational change leadership and advisory support for priority Technology initiatives, ensuring communications, stakeholder engagement, readiness, and adoption considerations are appropriately integrated into delivery plans.
Guide leaders and sponsors through periods of change by identifying employee impacts, adoption risks, stakeholder concerns, and readiness requirements, and recommending practical mitigation strategies.
Maintain Technology's OCM framework, methodologies, tools, and standards, ensuring a consistent and scalable approach to change management across major initiatives.
Monitor change readiness, adoption, stakeholder feedback, and employee impact across key initiatives, providing insights and recommendations to leadership.
Serve as an escalation point for significant communication, change, readiness, or employee-impact risks and advise leadership on appropriate actions.
Oversee the function's budget and vendor investments, ensuring resources are effectively managed and aligned to organizational priorities.

What You Will Bring

Bachelor's degree in Communications, Business Administration, Information Technology, Organizational Development, Change Management, or a related discipline.
Senior leadership experience within Technology, Communications, Organizational Change Management, Transformation, or a comparable strategic function in a complex organization.
Strong understanding of technology organizations, technology delivery, and the people, process, and adoption considerations required to successfully implement technology change.
Demonstrated experience advising senior executives and translating complex technology strategies, priorities, and initiatives into clear, actionable communications and engagement strategies.
Experience leading enterprise communications, executive communications, organizational change, employee engagement, or transformation initiatives across multiple stakeholder groups.
Strong understanding of change management principles, methodologies, and best practices, with experience applying them to technology-driven initiatives.
Experience providing strategic oversight and guidance on stakeholder engagement, impact assessment, readiness, adoption, communications, learning, and change risk management.
Proven ability to assess organizational impacts, competing priorities, stakeholder needs, and change implications and provide practical recommendations to leadership.
Ability to build strong partnerships and influence outcomes across Technology, Corporate Communications, HR, Enterprise Change, Learning, business leaders, and external partners.
Experience leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, including communications, change management, and external resources.
Exceptional communication, presentation, facilitation, stakeholder management, and leadership skills, with sound judgment in complex or high-visibility situations.
Experience managing budgets, vendor relationships, and external service providers.
Change Management certification (e.g., Prosci) is considered an asset.

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.

Description de poste:

Director, Enterprise Architecture Strategy, Core Platform

The Director, Enterprise Architecture Strategy is the architecture strategist supporting the Assistant Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, Core Platforms.

The Director drives the architecture integration strategy across cloud, on premise, network, application platforms, and foundational technology services. The role translates enterprise and business priorities into actionable architecture direction, roadmaps, investment priorities, standards, and modernization outcomes.

Working closely with the AVP, other Enterprise Architects, technology executives, engineering leaders, and domain and solution architects, the Director ensures that architecture priorities are aligned with business, operational, security, regulatory, and cost outcomes.

What will you do?

Working in collaboration with the other Enterprise Architects, define future-state architectures, transition roadmaps, principles, standards, reference architectures, and decision boundaries.
Provide strategic analysis, recommendations, visibility and executive reporting into architecture decisions, investments, dependencies, risks, and outcomes.
Maintain an integrated view of architecture priorities, decisions, dependencies, and outcomes.
Translate business priorities, executive direction, regulatory obligations, operational risks, and technology constraints into actionable architecture priorities.
Integrate cloud, infrastructure, network, security, identity, platform, API, and application architecture into a coherent enterprise direction.
Facilitate joint architecture planning and decision-making where initiatives cross business, portfolio, or technology boundaries.
Promote the reuse of enterprise capabilities, platforms, standards, patterns, and architecture decisions.
Escalate unresolved cross-domain decisions to the appropriate architecture or executive authority.
Lead architecture governance and ensure architecture decisions are documented, traceable, implementable, and aligned with security, resilience, operational, financial, and compliance requirements.
Partner with engineering and operational leaders to validate that architecture direction is practical, financially responsible, and sustainable in production.
Define and communicate measurable outcomes for technology health, risk reduction, resilience, cost efficiency, simplification and platform adoption.

What you'll need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business Technology Management, or a related discipline. A master’s degree is preferred.
Enterprise architecture credentials such as TOGAF, IASA CITA, or an equivalent architecture certification are preferred.
10 or more years of progressive architecture experience, including enterprise, portfolio, or cross-domain responsibility.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise technology strategies, future-state architectures, integrated roadmaps, standards, and transition plans.
Broad knowledge of cloud platforms, networks, operating systems, middleware, identity, security, virtualization, application hosting, APIs, integration, automation, and platform engineering.
Experience with cloud migration, infrastructure transformation, vulnerability remediation, technology currency, lifecycle management, and technical debt reduction.
Experience integrating architecture strategies and resolving dependencies across multiple business and technology domains.
Proven ability to influence senior business and technology leaders through clear analysis, options, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Ability to translate business and enterprise priorities into actionable architecture direction.
Ability to synthesize complex and fragmented information into a coherent enterprise position.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation, negotiation, and influence.
Strong financial and analytical acumen, including investment, cost, risk, and value trade-offs.
Ability to lead through influence, establish decision clarity, and resolve conflicts.
Sound judgment regarding when to standardize, consolidate, modernize, remediate, replace, retire, or accept risk.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
Working together, sharing common values, and encouraging growth & achievement.

new_jobs.title: Director, Technology Communications & Organizational Change Management (14 month contract)
new_jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Technology Communications & Change (14 month contract)
to lead two interconnected functions: Technology Communications and Technology Organizational Change Management (OCM). This role establishes the strategic direction, governance, standards, and priorities for how Technology communicates with employees, leaders, and external audiences, and how technology-driven change is assessed, planned, adopted, sustained, and measured across a complex portfolio of initiatives.

As a trusted advisor to Technology leadership, you will translate complex priorities into clear narratives, embed the employee perspective into critical decisions, and create the conditions required for successful organizational change. You will oversee portfolio-level change planning, strengthen sponsor and leadership capability, proactively identify change risk and organizational saturation, and ensure priority initiatives are supported by robust impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, learning, readiness, adoption, sustainment, and measurement practices that drive successful business outcomes.

What You Will Do

Define and drive the strategic direction for Technology communications and organizational change management, aligned with Technology priorities and business objectives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to Technology leadership, providing guidance on executive communications, employee engagement, organizational change, and stakeholder alignment.
Shape and oversee Technology's communications governance model, ensuring communication activities are coordinated, strategic, and aligned across the organization.
Partner closely with Corporate Communications, HR, Enterprise Change, Learning, Technology leaders, and business stakeholders to align messaging, coordinate change activity, and reduce communication overlap and fatigue.
Provide organizational change leadership and advisory support for priority Technology initiatives, ensuring communications, stakeholder engagement, readiness, and adoption considerations are appropriately integrated into delivery plans.
Guide leaders and sponsors through periods of change by identifying employee impacts, adoption risks, stakeholder concerns, and readiness requirements, and recommending practical mitigation strategies.
Maintain Technology's OCM framework, methodologies, tools, and standards, ensuring a consistent and scalable approach to change management across major initiatives.
Monitor change readiness, adoption, stakeholder feedback, and employee impact across key initiatives, providing insights and recommendations to leadership.
Serve as an escalation point for significant communication, change, readiness, or employee-impact risks and advise leadership on appropriate actions.
Oversee the function's budget and vendor investments, ensuring resources are effectively managed and aligned to organizational priorities.

What You Will Bring

Bachelor's degree in Communications, Business Administration, Information Technology, Organizational Development, Change Management, or a related discipline.
Senior leadership experience within Technology, Communications, Organizational Change Management, Transformation, or a comparable strategic function in a complex organization.
Strong understanding of technology organizations, technology delivery, and the people, process, and adoption considerations required to successfully implement technology change.
Demonstrated experience advising senior executives and translating complex technology strategies, priorities, and initiatives into clear, actionable communications and engagement strategies.
Experience leading enterprise communications, executive communications, organizational change, employee engagement, or transformation initiatives across multiple stakeholder groups.
Strong understanding of change management principles, methodologies, and best practices, with experience applying them to technology-driven initiatives.
Experience providing strategic oversight and guidance on stakeholder engagement, impact assessment, readiness, adoption, communications, learning, and change risk management.
Proven ability to assess organizational impacts, competing priorities, stakeholder needs, and change implications and provide practical recommendations to leadership.
Ability to build strong partnerships and influence outcomes across Technology, Corporate Communications, HR, Enterprise Change, Learning, business leaders, and external partners.
Experience leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, including communications, change management, and external resources.
Exceptional communication, presentation, facilitation, stakeholder management, and leadership skills, with sound judgment in complex or high-visibility situations.
Experience managing budgets, vendor relationships, and external service providers.
Change Management certification (e.g., Prosci) is considered an asset.

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.
